title: INDIAN NAVY COMMISSIONS INS MALVAN, THE SECOND OF THE MAHE-CLASS ANTI-SUBMARINE WARFARE SHALLOW WATER CRAFT
text:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau

Ministry of Defence

INDIAN NAVY COMMISSIONS INS MALVAN, THE SECOND OF THE MAHE-CLASS ANTI-SUBMARINE WARFARE SHALLOW WATER CRAFT

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
22 JUL 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi

INS Malvan, the second of the
 indigenously designed and built
 Mahe-class Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW-SWC), was commissioned at
Karwar on 22 Jul 2026.
 The event was presided over by
Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, Chief of the Air Staff,
 in the presence of Vice Admiral Sanjay Vatsayan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Western Naval Command. Other senior naval officers, representatives from Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL), Kochi, veterans, and distinguished guests were also in attendance.

The ship carries deep historical and cultural significance as it derives its name
from the historical coastal town of Malvan in Maharashtra, a region intrinsically linked to the illustrious maritime heritage of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
 The vessel also encapsulates the legacy of her predecessor, an inshore Indian Naval Minesweeper that remained in service till 2003.

INS Malvan is the second of eight ASW-SWCs, being indigenously built by CSL, Kochi,
 and the sixth of 16 ASW-SWCs to be commissioned into Indian Navy. With over
80 percent indigenous content,
 the ship reinforces the Government of India’s vision of
Aatmanirbhar Bharat
 and India’s expanding ecosystem of naval design, equipment, system integration, and growing self-reliance in defence shipbuilding.

The vessel is equipped for
Underwater Surveillance, Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) operations, and Low Intensity Maritime Operations (LIMO) along with Mine Warfare capability.
 The vessel will further bolster coastal defence, littoral security, and enhance Maritime Domain Awareness.

The crest of INS Malvan carries the ‘
Bagh Nakha’
(Tiger's Claw), symbolising bravery, warfare tactics, agility, and audacity, resonating with the ship's ethos to attack rapidly and strike silently.
 The waves surrounding
‘Bagh Nakha’
 reflect the vast sea surrounding the coasts and the Indian Navy's unwavering resolve to remain ever vigilant, ever ready, and steadfast in safeguarding the nation's seas and sovereignty.
The ship's motto,
‘Silent Claws’
, embodies lethality, stealth, and the ability to strike the adversary swiftly.

Addressing the gathering on the occasion, the Chief of the Air Staff emphasised the critical importance of safeguarding sea lines of communication to ensure unimpeded maritime trade amid global uncertainties. He lauded the Indian Navy's impressive growth and its commitment to the
Aatmanirbhar
 initiative, specifically highlighting the warship's over 80 percent indigenous content. Drawing inspiration from the Indian Navy's model of embedding officers directly into the shipbuilding process, he suggested that similar practices could accelerate self-reliance across the broader defence ecosystem. He also reaffirmed the vision of tri-service integration, calling for seamless jointness among the Indian Army, Indian Navy, and Indian Air Force to ensure the nation succeeds as one unified force in future conflicts.

The commissioning of INS Malvan adds a significant punch to the Indian Navy’s Anti-Submarine Warfare capabilities. With the ability to operate seamlessly with larger surface combatants, submarines, and aviation assets, induction of INS Malvan enables the Indian Navy to remain
Combat Ready, Credible, Cohesive, and Future Ready
 to ensure national security and safeguard India’s maritime interests at all times and at all locations.
